name: UF axion search
full_name: University of Florida early axion haloscope
summary: An early University of Florida resonant-cavity Galactic-halo axion experiment and an important precursor to later high-sensitivity searches.
detection_principle: A tunable high-Q cavity in a strong field is immersed in liquid helium; cryogenic HEMT amplifiers detect narrow axion-conversion spectral peaks.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 1990 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Results from a search for cosmic axions

collaboration.name: UF axion search Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Core configuration
key_parameters.value: Tunable high-Q cavity at liquid-helium temperature and cryogenic HEMT readout; numerical masses require verification against the full paper

results.summary: The 1990 result constrains axion coupling and Galactic abundance; no axions were observed.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.

media.caption: Schematic of the early University of Florida axion apparatus and receiver: tunable copper cavity in a superconducting magnet, liquid-helium environment, low-noise HEMT amplifier and mixer/FFT readout.
